gold: Complete changed tests and invoked setup helpers expose scenario-local fixture construction through the actual installed factory API. Prefer fitting native graph/include APIs over redundant preload wrappers, name child records before parent payloads, and preserve values, identities, nulls, persistence, ordering, lifecycle, and required preloads. Legitimate traits, necessary post-mutation reloads, reusable infrastructure, and libraries lacking equivalent APIs remain valid; structural or behavioral test success alone does not prove fixture compliance.

rubric.question: Inspect every complete changed test and its invoked setup helpers, including relevant hooks, factory traits, and association/lifecycle context, not only changed lines or helper names. A helper change requires the relevant caller scenarios needed to assess its contract. Missing required test/helper/context evidence yields BLOCKED with the exact missing prerequisite. Tests with no applicable fixture arrangement need no factory migration; explain their non-applicability rather than demanding unrelated dependencies.

Identify applicable shared/local fixture guidance and cite the actual resolved factory library/package version and supported API from installed documentation, types, or implementation matched to that version. Inspect relevant project factory definitions and model associations. A package declaration alone, an assumed API, or documentation for a different release is insufficient. If required API/version or guidance cannot be established, return BLOCKED rather than proposing a speculative replacement.

Determine whether the installed factory supports the scenario's child graph and required include/loading options. Cite a finding for a redundant reloadForIndexSerializer-style wrapper hiding scenario-specific association preloads or ordered collection loading when supported native APIs express the same contract. Name both the wrapper/call sites and the fitting API evidence. Do not accept a wrapper merely because tests pass, or invent unsupported graph/association features. Prefer explicit scenario-local native setup without replacing the wrapper with another opaque scenario builder.

Apply Function Calls Before Construction in docs/references/code-organization-reference.md#function-calls-before-construction to fixture setup: factory calls nested inside parent payload objects or association arrays receive a cited finding even when the native API is correct. Evaluate calls into descriptive scenario-local variables first, then reference the records in the parent payload. Preserve execution order, conditional scope, async awaiting, identities, and deliberate insertion order; named records before the parent call pass this criterion. Do not move persisted scenario setup into shared hooks or compress distinct meaningful records into opaque loops.

Compare original and corrected arrangements for exact scenario values/overrides, record identities and foreign keys, explicit nulls and deletion states, build versus create persistence, lifecycle timing, insertion order versus query order including deterministic tie-breakers, and all required preloads/nested associations. Preserve the action and meaningful assertions. Distinguish supplied child object identities from fresh instances returned by native loading; do not promise reference equality the API does not guarantee. Any semantic loss is a finding, even if naming, types, test behavior, or assertion counts pass.

Accept legitimate named opt-in owning-factory traits, reusable infrastructure, reloads required after mutation, and explicit creation/loading or justified helpers when the installed library lacks an equivalent API. Do not impose a universal factory/library mandate or a blanket helper/reload ban. Each FAIL finding must cite test/helper locations, governing guidance, installed API evidence, and a behavior-preserving correction. PASS requires complete applicable evidence and no unresolved findings; missing required evidence is BLOCKED. Prior structural/behavioral passes remain narrow evidence, not semantic clearance. After correction, assess the complete current scenario afresh through supported final review; this contract does not create a runtime, repair loop, or new advisor cadence.
